messages.subject: Warnings and Errors in JGR under Windows
messages.subject_clean: Warnings and Errors in JGR under Windows
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I notices some rather uncritical but annoying warning messages that  
appear in JGR but not in R's own GUI under Windows.

First is a quite harmless warning when starting JGR:

Beim Start - Warning messages:
1: 'Sys.putenv' ist veraltet.
Benutzen Sie stattdessen 'Sys.setenv'
Siehe help("Deprecated")

Second, I noticed warnings with object names that contain dots:
> My.Name <- c("Heinz", "Walter")
> My.Kuerzel <- c("H","W")
> My.Dat <- data.frame(My.Name, My.Kuerzel)
Warning messages:
1: '\.' ist eine unbekannte Escape-Sequenz in einer Zeichenkette
2: unbekannte Escape-Sequenz aus "data\.fr" entfernt
3: '\.' ist eine unbekannte Escape-Sequenz in einer Zeichenkette
4: unbekannte Escape-Sequenz aus "My\." entfernt
5: '\.' ist eine unbekannte Escape-Sequenz in einer Zeichenkette
6: unbekannte Escape-Sequenz aus "My\.K" entfernt

Once these names have been used in the session, the warning isn't shown again:
> My.Dat2 <- data.frame(My.Name, My.Kuerzel)
>

This doesn't really hurt, because everything works as expected, but it  
makes the output harder to read between the warning messages.

Besides these, I noticed an error with names that contain non-ascii  
characters:
> Kürzel <- c("H", "W")
Fehler: syntax error, unexpected $undefined, expecting '\n' or ';' in "Kü"
>

When giving names, one can surely avoid these characters. But when  
loading existing datasets, this makes variable access by name fail:
> load("test.RData")
> names(test)
[1] "Kürzel" "Name"
> test$Kürzel
Fehler: syntax error, unexpected $undefined, expecting '\n' or ';' in  
"Neuseeland.kat$Kü"


Cheers,
Frederik

messages.subject: JGR-15 launcher
messages.body_plain:
Using Vista, and having manually installed (using Rgui) the most current 
versions of iPlots / rJava / JavaGD / JGR from zip files obtained from 
Rforge today (24-Aug) , when I attempt to launch JGR using the new 
JGR-15.exe launcher also obtained from Rforge, the launcher still 
immediately attempts to update the above packages from a CRAN mirror and 
then opens a window explaining that the versions of those packages are 
too old, then quits. 

Given that in Windows the JGR package can only be run using the 
launcher, am I stuck waiting until the CRAN mirrors update these 
packages?  I tried to force the use of RForge as the repository by 
removing all other repository lines from the Repositories file, but the 
launcher still goes to CRAN.  I don't really understand why the launcher 
wants to update the packages at all, I would assume it would check 
package versions first but since I don't know how it does that ...

Thanks -- greatly appreciate that JGR has been updated to run under 
Vista.  I'm keen to test drive!

Joe

messages.subject: JGR and Windows Vista
messages.body_plain:
Simon or others:

Although JGR 1.5 is reportedly now running on Vista at least for Simon 
;) I haven't gained any ground in my quest to make this work.

Current versions:
Windows Vista Business 6.0 (build 6000)
R 2.5.1 (removed version 2.4.1, which was confusing the new JGR launcher)
Java 1.6.0_02 (also 1.5.0_12, 1.6, and 1.6.0)
JGR 1.5-4
rJava 0.5-0
JavaGD 0.4-3
iPlots 1.1-0

When I attempt to start JGR using the latest launcher, the splash screen 
displays, followed by the (Java) console window, which shows the startup 
of R 2.5.1, followed by the loading of packages rJava, JavaGD, and 
iPlots. (These packages are actually listed in sequence as loading 
twice).  Then a line "Error: \Uxxxxxxxx sequences are not supported on 
Windows.  Next line is the command prompt (>).  Immediately a Windows 
popup opens showing "Java (TM) 2 Platform Standard Edition binary has 
stopped working".  Program closes.

The same result occurs when launching using JGR debugging output; the 
failure occurs before any JGR debugging file is created.

Any clues about rectifying this situation much appreciated.  Anyone now 
successfully running JGR on Vista who can provides details of your 
installation -- I would be interested.

Joe
